questions.hint: Use Stirling numbers of the second kind.

questions.stem: Anchored by 12 and 5, how many equivalence relations on 12 elements have exactly 5 classes? Give the exact answer, based on the details given.
questions.explanation: Equivalence relations correspond to partitions, so the count is the Stirling number S(12,5)=1379400. Choosing a subset would ignore how the other elements are grouped.
questions.hint: Equivalence classes form a set partition.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: On the figure 4, how many binary relations are there on a set with 4 elements? State the correct choice, carefully.
questions.explanation: A relation is any subset of the n^2 ordered pairs, so there are 2^(4^2)=65536 relations. Counting functions or subsets of the set gives a much smaller number.
questions.hint: A relation is a subset of the Cartesian product.
